October 11

10 For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all. (James 2:10 KJV)

This verse makes it clear that those under the law must keep the whole law, and not just most of the law. If a person under the law fails to keep any one of the laws commandments, then he is guilty of breaking them all. God does not judge on the curve, and if you are in the top ten percent you get into heaven, but no, He judges on the complete law, and if you fail to keep one commandment, then you are guilty of breaking all the law. It is like a glass window, if it is broken, it has to be replaced, and it doesn’t matter how broken it is, it all has to be replaced. Remember that the law is not just the Ten Commandments, but it is hundreds of rules and regulations given by God. Anytime you are told you have to do certain actions, to be right with God, then you are being put under the law.

The preachers, who are teaching that you have to abide by the law, fail to take this verse into account, and many other verses that say you cannot be saved by keeping the law (Romans 3:20), as we have all failed to do so (Romans 3:10). Those that preach keeping the law are going to have to be judged by the law, and that means they are not going to be saved, as Paul wrote that keeping the law could save no one. Only one person was able to keep the whole law, and that was Jesus Christ, and He obtained the righteousness for us, and then gave it to us – Thank you Jesus!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
